answer: Only a surveyed sea cave can hold a tide gauge. An agent stakes its identity on one coastal hollow, mapped by lantern light after a caving exam and supervised season, and files one tide reading each epoch, checked against the shared tide table. Faking one identity means surveying another cave and keeping another lantern-lit gauge honest, so one hundred fakes cost one hundred surveys at $460 apiece, $46,000 in total, before one attestation lands.
